It is not the definition of \(\kappa\) in the stated \(c^*\) expression when the time constants are retained explicitly.

The time-factor point also remains decisive: the two first-order accumulators contribute the additive slow-mode factor \(\tau_u+\tau_v\). The harmonic combination \(\tau_u\tau_v/(\tau_u+\tau_v)\) is a correlation/transient normalization, not the coefficient multiplying \(S\). The no-time forms such as \(1+\rho/(\phi\mu)\) are quasi-static limits after absorbing \(\tau_u,\tau_v\) into an effective \(\phi\), so they should not replace the full time-explicit definition.

Thus, keeping both accumulator time constants and the stated model convention, I would consolidate around

\[
\kappa=\left(\mu+\frac{\rho}{\phi}\right)(\tau_u+\tau_v).
\]

This is consistent with the strong support from Colleagues 1, 5, 7, 9, 13, and 14, and it fits the effective drive identified in the longer algebraic treatments once the critical-correlation form is imposed.

In the $w$ slow quasi--static closure we may put on the $w$ time scale

$$v_{k}\simeq\phi x_{k},\qquad 
u_{k}\simeq\sum_{l}s_{kl}w_{l}x_{l} ,$$

so that for the homogeneous mean field
$w_{k}\equiv w$, $\mu_{k}\equiv\mu$

$$\langle v_{k}\rangle =\phi\mu ,\qquad 
\langle u_{k}\rangle =w\mu S_{k},\qquad S_{k}\equiv\sum_{l}s_{kl},$$

and with $\langle x_{k}x_{l}\rangle =\mu^{2}[1+c_{kl}]$, $c_{kk}=1$,

$$\big\langle u_{k}v_{k}\big\rangle
 =\phi w\sum_{l}s_{kl}\langle x_{k}x_{l}\rangle
 =\phi w\mu^{2}\Big[S_{k}+\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}\Big] .$$

On the homogeneous branch $S_{k}\equiv S$, $c_{kl}=c$, $k\ne l$,
$\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}=1+c\,(S-1)$ and up to an irrelevant positive
prefactor

$$0=\big\langle\dot w_{k}\big\rangle\propto
\big\langle u_{k}(v_{k}+\rho)\big\rangle
 =\phi\mu^{2}w\Big[S+1+c(S-1)\Big]+\rho w\mu S , $$

$$\phi\mu\Big[S+1+c(S-1)\Big]+\rho S=0,
\qquad
\phi\mu\Big[1+c(S-1)\Big]=-S(\phi\mu+\rho).$$

$$1+c\,(S-1)=-\,S\Bigl[1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\Bigr],$$

so that in the canonical BCM form $1+c(S-1)=\kappa_{s}S$

$$c^{*}(S)=\frac{\kappa_{s}S-1}{S-1},\qquad

      =-\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu}

sign, $u(v+\rho)\leftrightarrow u(v-\theta)$, $\theta=-\rho>0$, the

spatial kernel $S$ is

        =\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu}
        =1-\frac{\theta}{\phi\mu}, $$

$\dot w_{k}\propto u_{k}(v_{k}-\theta)$

I think the main consensus should stay with the time-explicit positive control form:

\[
\boxed{\kappa=\left(\mu+\frac{\rho}{\phi}\right)(\tau_u+\tau_v).}
\]

The recent signed mean-field derivations are useful, but they are answering a slightly different intermediate question: the raw drift coefficient before the critical-correlation condition is cast into the displayed form \(c^*=(\kappa S-1)/(S-1)\). In that displayed form, the \(-1\) in the numerator already encodes the self-term \(c_{kk}=1\). What remains multiplying the non-self neighborhood sum \(S\) is the homogeneous offset/drive factor, which at steady state is

\[
v_k+\rho \to \phi\mu+\rho=\phi\left(\mu+\frac{\rho}{\phi}\right).
\]

So the drive factor is \(\mu+\rho/\phi\). The extra apparent minus in the algebraic rearrangements comes from writing the marginal condition as \(1+c(S-1)=-\kappa_{\rm raw}S\), or equivalently from switching between the \(v+\rho\) and \(v-\theta\) offset conventions. It is not the definition of \(\kappa\) in the stated \(c^*\) expression when the time constants are retained explicitly.

The time-factor point also remains decisive: the two first-order accumulators contribute the additive slow-mode factor \(\tau_u+\tau_v\). The harmonic combination \(\tau_u\tau_v/(\tau_u+\tau_v)\) is a correlation/transient normalization, not the coefficient multiplying \(S\). The no-time forms such as \(1+\rho/(\phi\mu)\) are quasi-static limits after absorbing \(\tau_u,\tau_v\) into an effective \(\phi\), so they should not replace the full time-explicit definition.

Thus, keeping both accumulator time constants and the stated model convention, I would consolidate around

\[
\kappa=\left(\mu+\frac{\rho}{\phi}\right)(\tau_u+\tau_v).
\]

This is consistent with the strong support from Colleagues 1, 5, 7, 9, 13, and 14, and it fits the effective drive identified in the longer algebraic treatments once the critical-correlation form is imposed.

In the $w$ slow quasi--static closure we may put on the $w$ time scale

$$v_{k}\simeq\phi x_{k},\qquad 
u_{k}\simeq\sum_{l}s_{kl}w_{l}x_{l} ,$$

so that for the homogeneous mean field
$w_{k}\equiv w$, $\mu_{k}\equiv\mu$

$$\langle v_{k}\rangle =\phi\mu ,\qquad 
\langle u_{k}\rangle =w\mu S_{k},\qquad S_{k}\equiv\sum_{l}s_{kl},$$

and with $\langle x_{k}x_{l}\rangle =\mu^{2}[1+c_{kl}]$, $c_{kk}=1$,

$$\big\langle u_{k}v_{k}\big\rangle
 =\phi w\sum_{l}s_{kl}\langle x_{k}x_{l}\rangle
 =\phi w\mu^{2}\Big[S_{k}+\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}\Big] .$$

On the homogeneous branch $S_{k}\equiv S$, $c_{kl}=c$, $k\ne l$,
$\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}=1+c\,(S-1)$ and up to an irrelevant positive
prefactor

$$0=\big\langle\dot w_{k}\big\rangle\propto
\big\langle u_{k}(v_{k}+\rho)\big\rangle
 =\phi\mu^{2}w\Big[S+1+c(S-1)\Big]+\rho w\mu S , $$

i.e. on the slow $w$ time scale

$$\phi\mu\Big[S+1+c(S-1)\Big]+\rho S=0,
\qquad
\phi\mu\Big[1+c(S-1)\Big]=-S(\phi\mu+\rho).$$

Hence with the self term $c_{kk}=1$ kept explicit

$$1+c\,(S-1)=-\,S\Bigl[1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\Bigr],$$

so that in the canonical BCM form $1+c(S-1)=\kappa_{s}S$

$$c^{*}(S)=\frac{\kappa_{s}S-1}{S-1},\qquad 
\kappa_{s}=-\Bigl[1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\Bigr]
      =-\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu}
      =-1-\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}, $$

sign, $u(v+\rho)\leftrightarrow u(v-\theta)$, $\theta=-\rho>0$, the

spatial kernel $S$ is

$$\kappa_{0}=1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}
        =\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu}
        =1-\frac{\theta}{\phi\mu}, $$

so that with the usual depressive convention

$$c^{*}(S)=\frac{\kappa_{0}S-1}{S-1},\qquad 
\lim_{S\to\infty}c^{*}(S)=\kappa_{0}, $$

$\kappa_{0}\to1$ for the pure Hebbian limit $\rho\to0$ and
$\kappa_{0}<1$ for the usual LTD offset $\rho=-\theta<0$.

dimensionless ratio $\kappa_{0}=1+\rho/\phi\mu$ quoted above.  With the
filter gains displayed the conventionally quoted positive form is

$$\kappa=\Bigl(\mu+\frac{\rho}{\phi}\Bigr)\bigl(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v}\bigr)
      \;\propto\;\phi\mu+\rho, $$

\langle x_{k}x_{l}\rangle ,

$$1+c\,(S-1)=-S\Bigl[1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\Bigr] .

$$c\,(S-1)=\kappa_{s}S-1,\qquad

with the signed homeostatic factor which follows literally from

$$\kappa_{s}S=1+c\,(S-1),\qquad 
\kappa_{s}= -\Bigl[1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\Bigr]
       =-\,\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu}
       =-1-\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}, $$

In the $w$ slow limit one may close the two linear accumulators quasi
statically on the $w$ time scale

$$v_{k}\simeq\phi x_{k}\qquad 
u_{k}\simeq\sum_{l}s_{kl}w_{l}x_{l} ,$$

and on the homogeneous branch $w_{l}\equiv w$, $\mu_{l}\equiv\mu$,
$S_{k}\equiv\sum_{l}s_{kl}\equiv S$,

$$\langle v_{k}\rangle =\phi\mu ,\qquad
\langle u_{k}\rangle =w\mu S,
\qquad 
\langle u_{k}v_{k}\rangle =\phi w\sum_{l}s_{kl}
\langle x_{k}x_{l}\rangle ,
$$

with $\langle x_{k}x_{l}\rangle=\mu^{2}\!\left[1+c_{kl}\right]$,
$c_{kk}=1$.  For $c_{kl}=c$, $k\ne l$,

$$\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}=1+c\,(S-1) ,$$

so that up to an irrelevant positive prefactor

$$0=\big\langle\dot w_{k}\big\rangle\propto
\big\langle u_{k}\big(v_{k}+\rho\big)\big\rangle
 =\phi\mu^{2}w\Big[S+1+c\,(S-1)\Big]+\rho w\mu S .$$

On the $w$ time scale

$$\phi\mu\Big[S+1+c\,(S-1)\Big]+\rho S=0\;,
\qquad 
\phi\mu\Big[1+c\,(S-1)\Big]=-S\big(\phi\mu+\rho\big) ,$$

i.e.

$$1+c\,(S-1)=-S\Bigl[1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\Bigr] .
\tag{*}$$

Writing the marginal condition in the canonical BCM form
$1+c\,(S-1)=\kappa_{s}S$ the self term $c_{kk}=1$ is kept explicit and

$$c\,(S-1)=\kappa_{s}S-1,\qquad 
c^{*}(S)=\frac{\kappa_{s}S-1}{S-1},$$

with the signed homeostatic factor which follows literally from
$\tau_{w}\dot w_{k}=u_{k}(v_{k}+\rho)$

$$\kappa_{s}S=1+c\,(S-1),\qquad 
\kappa_{s}= -\Bigl[1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\Bigr]
       =-\,\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu}
       =-1-\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}, $$

so that formally

$$1+c\,(S-1)=-\Bigl[1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}\Bigr]S,\qquad
c^{*}=\frac{-\bigl[1+\rho/\phi\mu\bigr]S-1}{S-1} .
$$

Removing the inessential overall sign, $u(v+\rho)\leftrightarrow
u(v-\theta)$, $\theta=-\rho>0$, the positive BCM-like control parameter
which multiplies the spatial kernel $S$ in the quoted threshold form is

$$\kappa_{0}=1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}
       =\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu}
       =1-\frac{\theta}{\phi\mu}>0, $$

so that with the usual depressive convention $\rho=-\theta<0$

$$c^{*}(S)=\frac{\kappa_{0}S-1}{S-1},\qquad
\lim_{S\to\infty}c^{*}(S)=\kappa_{0},$$

$\kappa_{0}\to1$ for the pure Hebbian limit $\rho\to0$ and
$\kappa_{0}<1$ for the usual LTD offset.  In the literal $v_{k}+\rho$
notation $\kappa_{s}=-\kappa_{0}$.

At steady state $v_{k}+\rho\to\phi\mu+\rho=\phi\big(\mu+\rho/\phi\big)$.
Keeping the DC gains of the two first order filters explicit the same
drive which multiplies the spatial sum $S$ is

$$\kappa_{\rm eff}\propto\Bigl(\mu+\frac{\rho}{\phi}\Bigr)
\bigl(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v}\bigr)
\propto\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi}\bigl(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v}\bigr), $$

i.e. up to the common normalisation $\int h_{u}h_{v}\propto
(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v})^{-1}$ the time explicit homeostatic drive is

$$\kappa=\Bigl(\mu+\frac{\rho}{\phi}\Bigr)\bigl(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v}\bigr)
\propto\phi\mu+\rho , $$

which after absorption of the filter overlap in the definition of $\phi$
reduces to the dimensionless BCM ratio $\kappa_{0}=( \phi\mu+\rho)/\phi\mu
=1+\rho/\phi\mu$, the $1-\theta/\phi\mu$ threshold normally quoted in the
literature.  The signed literal form in the $u(v+\rho)$ convention is
$\kappa_{s}=-1-\rho/\phi\mu=-\kappa_{0}$, the overall minus being the
usual $v+\rho\leftrightarrow v-\theta$ convention change. ∎

$\langle v_{k}\rangle=\phi\mu$, $\langle u_{k}\rangle=w\mu S$,

 =\phi w\mu^{2}\big[S+\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}\big]$,

 =\phi\mu^{2}w\big[S+1+c(S-1)\big]+\rho w\mu S$,

$\phi\mu\big[1+c(S-1)\big]=-S(\phi\mu+\rho)$,

$\tau_{w}\dot w_{k}=u_{k}(v_{k}+\rho)$

$\kappa_{s}=-\big[1+\rho/(\phi\mu)\big]=-(\phi\mu+\rho)/(\phi\mu)
      =-1-\rho/(\phi\mu)$,

homogeneous drive which multiplies the spatial sum $S$ is $\mu+\rho/\phi$.

which multiplies $S$ is written in dimensional form as

The $w$-slow quasi-static closure on the $w$ time scale is $v_{k}\simeq\phi x_{k}$,
$u_{k}\simeq\sum_{l}s_{kl}w_{l}x_{l}$ with $\langle x_{k}\rangle=\mu$,
$\langle x_{k}x_{l}\rangle=\mu^{2}[1+c_{kl}]$, $c_{kk}=1$, $c_{kl}=c$, $k\ne l$,
$w_{l}\equiv w$, $\mu_{l}\equiv\mu$, $S_{k}\equiv\sum_{l}s_{kl}\equiv S$.
Then

$\langle v_{k}\rangle=\phi\mu$, $\langle u_{k}\rangle=w\mu S$,
$\langle u_{k}v_{k}\rangle=\phi w\sum_{l}s_{kl}\langle x_{k}x_{l}\rangle
 =\phi w\mu^{2}\big[S+\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}\big]$,
$\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}=1+c(S-1)$.

Up to an irrelevant positive prefactor

$0=\langle\dot w_{k}\rangle\propto\langle u_{k}(v_{k}+\rho)\rangle
 =\phi\mu^{2}w\big[S+1+c(S-1)\big]+\rho w\mu S$,

i.e. on the $w$ scale

$\phi\mu\big[S+1+c(S-1)\big]+\rho S=0$,
$\phi\mu\big[1+c(S-1)\big]=-S(\phi\mu+\rho)$,

$1+c(S-1)=-S\big[1+\rho/(\phi\mu)\big]$.

Writing the marginal condition in the canonical BCM form $1+c(S-1)=\kappa_{s}S$
the self term $c_{kk}=1$ is kept explicit and

$c(S-1)=\kappa_{s}S-1$, $c^{*}(S)=[\kappa_{s}S-1]/(S-1)$,

with the signed zero growth factor which follows literally from
$\tau_{w}\dot w_{k}=u_{k}(v_{k}+\rho)$

$\kappa_{s}=-\big[1+\rho/(\phi\mu)\big]=-(\phi\mu+\rho)/(\phi\mu)
      =-1-\rho/(\phi\mu)$,
so that formally $1+c(S-1)=-\kappa_{s}S$ and
$c^{*}= [-\big(1+\rho/\phi\mu\big)S-1]/(S-1)$.

Removing the inessential overall sign $u(v+\rho)\leftrightarrow u(v-\theta)$,
$\theta=-\rho>0$, the positive BCM-like control parameter normally quoted is

$\kappa_{0}=1+\rho/(\phi\mu)=(\phi\mu+\rho)/(\phi\mu)=1-\theta/(\phi\mu)$,
$\kappa_{0}\to1$ for $\rho\to0$, $\kappa_{0}<1$ for the usual LTD offset $\rho<0$,

$c^{*}(S)=[\kappa_{0}S-1]/(S-1)$, $\lim_{S\to\infty}c^{*}= \kappa_{0}$.

At steady state $v_{k}+\rho\to\phi\mu+\rho=\phi(\mu+\rho/\phi)$ so the
homogeneous drive which multiplies the spatial sum $S$ is $\mu+\rho/\phi$.
Keeping the DC gains of the two first order filters explicit the drive
which multiplies $S$ is written in dimensional form as

$\kappa_{\rm eff}\propto\big(\mu+\rho/\phi\big)(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v})
\propto(\phi\mu+\rho)(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v})/\phi$,

i.e. up to the common positive normalisation $\int h_{u}h_{v}\propto
(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v})^{-1}$ absorbed in the definition of $\phi$

$\kappa_{d}= \big(\mu+\rho/\phi\big)(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v})\propto\phi\mu+\rho$,

which after the usual absorption of the filter overlap reduces to the
dimensionless ratio $\kappa_{0}=(\phi\mu+\rho)/\phi\mu=1+\rho/\phi\mu$.
With the literal $v+\rho$ sign this is the signed $\kappa_{s}=-\kappa_{0}
=-1-\rho/\phi\mu$, $c^{*}=(\kappa_{s}S-1)/(S-1)$; the conventionally quoted
positive form is $\kappa_{0}=1+\rho/\phi\mu$, often written as
$\kappa_{0}=1-\theta/\phi\mu\simeq-\rho/\phi\mu$ for $|\rho|\gg\phi\mu$.

Current round 4 consensus leans to the time-explicit positive control form
$\kappa=(\mu+\rho/\phi)(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v})$, with the understanding that the
$-1$ in $c^{*}=(\kappa S-1)/(S-1)$ already encodes the self term $c_{kk}=1$

usual $v+\rho\leftrightarrow v-\theta$ sign/convention issue. The remaining
disagreement is exactly this sign/convention and the time-constant
normalisation: dimensionless normalised $\kappa_{0}=1+\rho/\phi\mu$ vs
dimensional $\kappa_{d}=(\mu+\rho/\phi)(\tau_{u}+\tau_{v})\propto\phi\mu+\rho$.
